texts.preamble: Mukut Lal vs The State ( Govt Of Nct Of Delhi ) on 15 January, 2021 The Court Of Shri Anil Antil Additional Sessions Judge-04, New Delhi District Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Criminal Appeal Number : 56/2017 Cc No. : 04/2001 U/S: : 16(1)(a) r/w Section 7 of P.F.A Act-1954 Mukut Lal, s/o ShChhokanLal, r/o 8/7384, 4th Floor, East Gorakh Park, Gali no. 11, Shahdara, Delhi .....Appellant versus The State ( Govt of Nct of Delhi ) through Department of Prevention of Food Adulteration, Office at : A-20, Lawrence Road, Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 .....Respondent
texts.facts: Benefit of Section 428 Cr.P.C, if any, applicable was given to him. 3. The brief facts of the present case are that on 30.08.2000, the Food Inspectors Sh. Jeet Ram and Sh. S.K. Gupta under the supervision of Local Health Authority/SDM Sh. Satnam Singh reached at the premises M/s Balaji Sweet Corner at 128 Railway Road, Shahadra, Delhi-32, where accused/appellant was found conducting business of various food articles which were lying stored for sale for human consumption ; - that FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of 'Burfee' from the vendor which was lying in open tray bearing no label declaration, to which he agreed ; CA no. 56/17 Mukut Lal Vs. Vs. The State / DA - that thereafter as per the prescribed procedure under the PFA Act and Rules after giving notice to the vendor/appellant and offer towards the sale price of sample to which he agreed and accepted the sale consideration, sample was then lifted ; that each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked, sealed and necessary documents including Notice as per Form-VI in the presence of appellant/accused alongwith Panchnama etc was prepared at the spot ; the price of the sample commodity was paid to the vendor ; - that thereafter one counterpart of sample was sent to Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA ; - that vide report dated 15.09.2000, PA found the sample to be adulterated not conforming to the standards on the grounds that it contained vegetable oil which was not declared as an ingredient ; - that upon receipt of report, SDM/LHA directed investigation which was carried out by Food Inspector and after completion of investigation sanction under Section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 14.05.2001 alleging violation of Section 2(ia),(a),(b),(c) and (m) of PFA Act punishable under Section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA. Act. - that the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, hence, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with ; 4. The appellant/accused was summoned by the learned trial court vide order dated 14.05.2001 for 20.08.2001 to face trial. Mukut Lal vs The State ( Govt Of Nct Of Delhi ) on 15 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25081329/ 2 After filing his appearance, the appellant opted to file an application under section 13(2) of the PFA Act and moved CA no. 56/17 Mukut Lal Vs. Vs. The State / DA appropriate application thereby exercising right to get the second counterpart of the sample analyzed from the Central Food Laboratory (CFL). The application was allowed and counterpart was directed to be sent to the CFL for analysis. The sample was examined by the Director CFL and he gave his certificate dated 09.07.2001 opining the sample to be adulterated on the ground that it contained vegetable oil. 5. Thereafter matter was listed for pre-charge evidence, wherein the complainant examined PW-1 Sh. Jeet Ram, Food Inspector. 6. On the basis of testimony of PW-1 on 04.08.2008 charge was framed against the appellants/accused for commission of offences punishable u/s 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act for violation of provisions of Section 2(ia)(a),(j) and (m) of PFA Act alleging therein that on 30.08.2000 at about 05.00 p.m, the appellant being the the Vendor cum Proprietor of M/s Balaji Sweet Corner, 128 Railway Road, Shahdara, Delhi-32 was found vending various food article including Burfee and sold its sample of about 1500 grams for analysis bearing no label or declaration ready for sale, taken from an open tray to Food Inspector on payment of sample commodity in the presence of LHA and witnesses and it was analyzed by Public Analyst vide Certificate No. G14-4/2001-230 dated 09.07.2007 and it was found that the sample is adulterated because added colour i.e. 2.2ppm tartrazine present, vegetable oil present and thereby violated the provisions of Section 2(ia)(a)(j) and (m) of PFA Act, and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 16(1)(a) of CA no. 56/17 Mukut Lal Vs. Vs. The State / DA PFA Act, 1954 read with Section 7 of the PFA Act to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 6.1 During trial after the examination and detailed cross examination of witnesses of the department i.e. PW1 Sh. Jeet Ram, Food Inspector, PW2 Ms. Suniti Kumar Gupta and PW3 Sh.Satnam Singh, Secretary, APMC,GMNCT of Delhi the then SDM/LHA, prosecution evidence was closed and matter was fixed for Statement of accused. 7. The statement of appellant/accused was recorded under section 313 Cr.PC in which he pleaded his innocence and stated that no efforts were made by the Food Inspector to join public witnesses no price was paid by the Food Inspector, sample was not sent in his presence, the tray was pasted by vegetable oil to avoid sticking of Burfee with the tray ; complaint was filed a routine manner, CFL report is wrong he did not apply his proper method of analyzing the sample, it is a false case ; he was not selling any food item having khoya as ingredient ; under the pressure and duress he made endorsement on Ex PW1/B The burfee was made from left out items such as besan, maida sugar and khaand and he preferred to lead defence evidence but despite opportunities no defence witness was examined. 9.(I) The appellant has assailed the judgment and order on sentence passed by the learned trial court by urging various grounds. 10. During the course of argument on 06.01.2021, learned counsel for the appellant submitted that appellant is not challenging the merits of the case/ conviction decided by the learned trial court vide judgment dated 28.02.2017 and is confining his appeal limited to the quantum of sentence only, awarded to him vide order dated 01.03.2017 ; and to confirm his submissions appellant has tender his statement in this regard and prayed that a lenient view be taken against him by giving him the benefit of New Legislation as FSSAI.
texts.arguments: II) Alternatively, on the quantum of sentence, relying upon the new legislation, it was pleaded that the case of the appellant be considered sympathetically in the light of the preposition of law laid down by the Hon'ble Courts pursuant to coming of new legislation that is Food Safety & Standards Act. Learned counsel for the Delhi Admn./Food Department, objected to the same and submitted that according to statement of appellant, prosecution has established its case and he be sentenced with strict punishment in terms of old Act wherein minimum punishment is prescribed and no leniency should be shown to the convict as it is a serious offence of food adulteration article / commodity leading to hazardous consequences on the health or body of a person. 12. I have carefully gone through the available record as well as trial court record, have heard the submissions of learned counsel for both the parties at length and have also gone through the judgments relied upon by the parties. 13. It is argued by learned counsel for the appellant that on the date of pronouncement of judgment/order on sentence, the PFA Act, 1954 was repealed and new act had come into operation. It is stated that the court should give benefit of the new legislation to the accused vide which the punishment provided under the old act has been diluted to a considerable extent, and that the offence for which CA no. 56/17 Mukut Lal Vs. Vs. The State / DA the accused/appellant has been convicted now falls under the category of "Unsafe Food" punishable under section 59 of the new Act i.e Food and Safety Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter called FSSAI) punishable only with fine upto Rs. Five lacs. 15. It was argued by learned counsel for the appellant that appellant is respectable person of society, has deep roots in the society, has responsibility towards his family, not involved in any other case, suffering from some diseases, has no other source of income except vegetable selling and prayed that a lenient view be taken against him in the light of the provisions of law under the new Act. 15.1 Further that case pertains to the year 2006, the appellant/accused has faced the trial almost 14 years which by itself is a sufficient punishment and the hardships faced by him has caused him great mental agony, stress and rigors of trial during the said period. It is also stated that now a days special circumstances exists due to outbreak of pandemic of Covid-19 and there are chances of appellant being infected with virus in case imprisonment of sentence is awarded to him. 15.2 In support of his submissions, learned counsel for appellant had relied upon the judgment of Nemi Chand Vs. State of Rajasthan ( Crl. Appeals No. 214 and 215 of 2016, vide order dated 10.03.2016, as corrected vide order dated 17.03.2016, as reported in 2016 (1) FAC 203 ) of Hon'ble Supreme Court and earlier judgment T Barai Vs. Henry 1983 ( ) SCC 177. 15.3 Per contra, learned SPP, strongly opposed the submissions CA no. 56/17 Mukut Lal Vs. Vs. The State / DA advanced by learned counsel by addressing that the sentencing cannot be done in new Act since the definition of many offences are changed in the new Act including this particular offence of which accused is charged. Definition of major offences like "adulteration" and "misbranding" have been changed. Now FSSAI have definition "substandard food", "food containing extraneous matter" "unsafe food" and misbranded food". Due to this reason, the ingredients have changed and thus there is no way in which the old offences could be related to new offences. The relevant portion of the T Barai Judgment is as follows : - (Para 25) It is settled both on authority and principle that when a later statute again describes an offence created by an earlier statute and imposes a different punishment or varies the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by implication in Michell Vs. Brown ( 1958) 120 ER 909, 912 : 32 LTOS 146:7 WR 80 Lord Campbell put the matter thus : - "It is well settled rule of construction that, if a later statute again describes an ofence created by a former statute and affixes a different punishment, varying the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by the later statute see also Smith Vs. Benabo ( 1937) 1 ALL ER 523 : ( 1997) 1 KB 518: 156 LT 194" - In Regina Vs. Youle ( 1861) 158 ER 311,315-16 : LT 299 : 9 CA no. 56/17 Mukut Lal Vs. Vs. The State / DA WR 637 Martin B. said in the oft-quoted passage : - If a statute deals with a particular class of offences, and a subsequent Act is passed which deals with precisely the same offence, and a different punishment is imposed by the later Act, I think that, in effect, the legislature has declared that the new Act shall be substituted for the earlier Act." - Moreover, this particular aspect is stated as a illustration in the same judgment in Para 23 which is as follows : Mukut Lal vs The State ( Govt Of Nct Of Delhi ) on 15 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25081329/ 6 - To illustrate, if Parliament were to reenact Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and provide that the punishment for an offence of murder shall be sentence for imprisonment for life instead of the present sentence of death or imprisonment for life, then it can not be that the courts would still award a sentence of death even in pending cases. Vide said letter the said authority, in the light of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Nemi Chand's Case (supra) issued an advisory to the Commissioners of Food Safety/Officers incharge of Food Safety to dispose of the long pending court cases filed under old PFA Act CA no. 56/17 Mukut Lal Vs. Vs. The State / DA mainly concerning substandard and misbranding by imposing fine only.
